prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset: production sprite atlas for Cosmic: A Sea Beneath the Moon. Input image1 is a STYLE reference only: retain the medallion form, palette, grain and physical depiction approach, but create the NEW requested subjects below. Exactly 4 columns by 4 rows, 16 circles total. Regular equal square cells, Use a SQUARE canvas, exactly 4 columns by 4 rows, equal square cells, no outer margin. Aim2048px wide. Every circle diameter84%of its cell, centred, with generous fully transparent gutters; leave allcells complete and separated. No extra cells or objects. Original astronomical chromolithograph with dry-gouache and chalk masses: deep indigo circular fields, feathered warm-ivory light, amber heat, copper/charcoal minerals and restrained teal water. Simplify to broad meaningful structures visible at72px. Fine grain stays in subjects; generous quiet dark space. One thin ivory circular outline. No glossy UI buttons, photographic lens flare, ornamental decoration, humans, machines, text, labels, numerals, formulas or grid lines. Inside each circle the field is opaque; outside circles true alpha transparency. No shadows, rays or fragments beyond circles. Atom/particle diagrams are schematic: tiny compact ivory dots and diffuse electron-probability clouds, never planetary electron orbits; individual nuclei do NOT glow like stars. Exact invisible chemistry is communicated by game names/readings, never by invented diagnostic coloration. All terrestrial worlds have bare mineral terrain; no plants, life or modern continents. Early Moon is pale gray-ivory without familiar dark maria. All Earth cutaways are views of one continuing world.
Strict row-major subjects (left to right, then top to bottom):
1. Hot inner orbits: A close arc of the solar disk beside a cropped warm Sun, lit strongly from the inner edge. Avoid: A location within a disk, no solid orbital rail or ice.
2. Cold outer orbits: A broad dim outer disk arc with the small Sun distant across a large dark central gap. Avoid: Distance and lighting carry distinction; no sharply painted snow-line ring.
3. Brief intense heating: A small rocky aggregate briefly rimmed by a broad intense amber flare, surrounding space remaining dark. Avoid: Heat pulse without invented lightning, machinery or a settled heating mechanism.
4. Hot inner-disk vapor: A diffuse bright amber wisp above the inner arc of the solar disk, no surviving hard grains in the centre. Avoid: State and hot location are visible; vapor composition cannot be read by colour alone.
5. Refractory mineral grains: A small loose cluster of pale angular condensed mineral facets with a faint cooling glow behind. Avoid: Angular grains rather than frozen rounded droplets; exact refractory chemistry needs label.
6. A rocky dust aggregate: One porous irregular clump built from visibly joined angular grains with small dark gaps. Avoid: Loose joined structure, not a monolithic rock or compact planet.
7. Molten rocky droplets: Three separated round amber droplets with smooth glowing edges and dark space between. Avoid: Molten silicate droplets glow; metal droplets belong inside a surrounding melt.
8. Cooled chondrules: Three cooled charcoal rounded grains, broken pale mineral textures visible across their faces. Avoid: Round solids with no heat glow; do not turn them into cratered planets.
9. A mixture of stone and metal: A loose sample of rounded chondrules, angular fine rock and two metallic glints, no common outer body. Avoid: Distinct constituent shapes remain separate; no ice mantle.
10. Water vapor in warm orbits: A dark grain losing its pale mantle into a thin diffuse wisp near a warm disk arc. Avoid: Sublimation is a schematic transition; no liquid drops floating in a vacuum.
11. Recondensed outer-disk ice: Two dark grain cores with newly forming continuous pale rims in a dim outer-disk arc. Avoid: Same water ice appearance as inherited ice; context records its different history.
12. An outer-disk store of ice and dust: A broad loose sample of pale ice-mantled grains mixed with dark rocky dust. Avoid: Unjoined reservoir of solids; neither a snowbank nor icy finished world.
13. Gentle grain collisions: Two small porous grains meet at one slight contact point, with short quiet inward motion strokes. Avoid: No shards, fiery explosion or guaranteed perfect sticking at all speeds.
14. Drag from orbiting gas: Several dark pebbles cross a pale curved gas stream with their short paths deflected slightly inward. Avoid: Distributed flow interaction; no wind fan or mechanical braking device.
15. A pressure maximum in the disk: Two broad gas-stream arcs converge toward one dense narrow curved band of pebbles. Avoid: A smooth concentration region, not a physical fence or rail.
16. Gravity within a dense swarm: A dense loose swarm of grains has three short inward cues toward its common centre. Avoid: Mutual attraction across many solids; no finished planet at centre.
